title: Consolidated Hosted Bundle: Behavior Profiles PRD + Launch Checklist
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description: This PRD defines a consolidated behavior profile bundle for Redwood hosted endpoints that standardizes contracts and launch acceptance across four interaction surfaces: chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank. Goal: ship a minimal, interoperable set of behavior guarantees and operational runbooks so customers can migrate from ad-hoc endpoints to a single, predictable surface with clear cost/latency/quality tradeoffs. The bundle includes: behavioral contracts, deterministic sampling mode for reproducible completions, embedding normalization and dimensionality guarantees, rerank stability constraints, compatibility fallbacks, canary rollout plan, telemetry and SLO thresholds, and ops runbooks for degraded modes and rollbacks.
scope_clarifications: Included surfaces: chat (multi-turn stateful), completions (single-turn generative), embeddings (vector generation + normalization), rerank (pairwise/document ranking).
Supported model classes: Redwood-verified open models and canonical quantized variants designated in the model catalog; model-specific tuning outside scope.
Interface contract: REST/SDK endpoints with unified auth and per-route config; no changes to tokenization behavior except documented normalization for embeddings.
Data retention: platform telemetry only (no customer prompt retention changes); Private deployments follow customer KMS and audit controls separately.
non_goals: Providing new model training or fine-tuning APIs.
Comprehensive CLI or Terraform controls for Dedicated capacity (only minimal config exposed).
Changing existing hosted billing primitives (billing/units unchanged).
scope_changes_log: 2025-02-12: Removed 'session-level persistent KV' from initial launch scope due to dependency on ENG-18432's storage contract (dependency added).
2025-02-14: Reduced initial canary coverage target from 10% to 5% after SRE requested additional tracing instrumentation (see dependency ENG-19102).
2025-02-17: Added deterministic sampling mode as a must-have after customer feedback from enterprise pilot (impact on SDKs and acceptance criteria).
acceptance_criteria: Functional: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints accept the defined payloads and return 200/JSON schema-conformant responses for 99% of synthetic testcases.

Quality: evaluation harness shows no more than 3% regression in ranking NDCG@10 for rerank vs baseline model on lighthouse dataset; embeddings cosine stability >= 0.98 across 1000 sample permutations after normalization.
Performance: p95 latency for completions (short prompt median length=64 tokens) <= 200ms in hosted-std lane at steady state under production-like load; embeddings p95 <= 180ms.
Cost: average token compute cost deviation <= 12% of predicted cost model across a 72-hour smoke run with representative traffic (batching enabled).
Reliability: error rate across surfaces <= 1% for successful request processing during canary; degradation policy enacted automatically above 3% error rate.
Determinism: deterministic sampling mode reproduces token sequences within 1 token variance across 10 repeated runs for deterministic seeds (where model supports determinism).

Operational: Console dashboards expose per-route token cost, latency heatmap, canary slice metrics, and a 'graded degradation' toggle; alerts wired for latency SLO breach, error rate spike, and quality regression alerts tied to eval-suite thresholds.
launch_checklist: Final PRD signoff by Product, SRE, and Security.
SDK updates released: Python/Node patch with deterministic flag and schema changes (release notes drafted).
E2E tests added to CI: synthetic scenarios for chat turns, embeddings dimensionality, rerank stability; green for 3 consecutive runs.
Canary plan scheduled: day-0 5% of traffic for 24h, day-1 expand to 25% (if SLOs met), day-3 full rollout pending quality gates.
Telemetry: per-route traces and user-level sampling enabled; cost telemetry validated against accounting pipeline.
Ops runbook published and linked in Console (runbook includes rollback steps and degraded-mode policy).
Safety & compliance checklist complete: data-flow diagrams, threat model review, and security signoff.
Support playbook: Level 1/2 triage steps, escalation contacts, and canned responses for known issues.
rollout_strategy: Canary with staged expansion and automatic fallback. Start with 5% of production traffic to the new bundle for 24 hours; monitor latency/error/quality gates. If all gates pass, expand to 25% for 48 hours; if still healthy, expand to 100% on day 4. Auto-fallback to previous endpoint variants when error rate > 3% for 5 minutes or when quality regression alert triggers (NDCG drop > threshold).
ops_and_rollback: Immediate rollback command: /ops/traffic-swap to previous revision (run by SRE on call).
Degraded mode policy: switch chat to 'fast-mode' (lower max tokens, stricter batching) when p95 exceeds 2x target for more than 10 minutes.
Postmortem requirement: SLA-impacting incidents require a 72-hour postmortem and mitigation plan.
monitoring_and_slos: SLOs: availability >= 99.9% (monthly), latency p95 as defined in acceptance criteria per surface.
Quality gates: rerank NDCG baseline delta <= -3%, embeddings stability >= 0.98, completions topical coherence pass rate >= 92% on eval set.
Dashboards: per-model and per-route latency percentiles, errors by class, token cost burn, eval-suite trendlines.
risk_assessment: Model variance: different open models produce output drift; mitigated by pinned model variants and canarying per-catalog entry.
Telemetry gaps: missing signals could hide regressions; we require instrumentation before canary expansion.
Cost overshoot: unexpected batching behavior could increase per-token compute; pre-launch 72-hour smoke-run required.
post_launch_tasks: Collect 7-day traffic quality report and compare to pre-launch baseline; schedule review with Research/Applied ML.
Migrate customer pilot tenants to consolidated endpoints with opt-in instructions and support window.
Iterate on deterministic sampling UX in SDKs based on early feedback.
